name: Matthat
overview: Matthat is a male figure noted in the lineage of the Messiah, as recorded in Luke 3:29. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not specified, his inclusion in this genealogy highlights his role in the ancestral line leading to Christ. No further notes are provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Matthat means "gift" or "something given," reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This meaning may imply a recognition of divine blessing or provision, though the name itself was not given directly by God. The name appears explicitly in Luke 3:29.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Matthat as the son of Jorim and the father of Levi, establishing his place within a familial lineage. These relationships are noted explicitly or inferred in Luke 3:29. Beyond these connections, no additional family details are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Matthat's significance lies primarily in his position within the genealogical record of Jesus Christ, marking him as an ancestor in the Messiah's human ancestry. This connection underscores the fulfillment of God's promises through the lineage traced in Luke. While the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his inclusion affirms the historical and theological continuity leading to Christ.
